target_customer: Business teams and analysts at startups and mid-size companies needing dashboards from SQL databases
problem: Teams had data in MySQL and PostgreSQL but needed engineers or expensive BI tools to chart it. Chartio offered cloud dashboards without SQL.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for cloud business intelligence
product_category: Cloud business intelligence and data visualization

founders.name: Dave Fowler
founders.background_notes: YC page and Atlassian announcement name Dave Fowler as founder and CEO; no biography in opened sources. One aggregator names a second founder, Daniel Levine, not verified.

competitors.name: RJMetrics
competitors.what: Hosted analytics for e-commerce and SaaS

technical_complexity.rationale: Connectors to customer databases, a query builder that hides SQL and fast charting on live data are standard but demanding engineering, done by a very small team at launch.

defensibility.rationale: Dashboards and saved queries created some lock-in, but many cloud BI tools did similar things and Tableau, Looker and others competed for the same buyers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent BI vendors did not buy it. Atlassian acquired it in February 2021 and retired the product on 1 March 2022.

market_need_then: Companies with SQL databases lacked self-serve charting; the 2010 TechCrunch launch coverage frames the product as a simple alternative to heavier BI, though the sources give no spend figures.

branding.domain_note: Launched as Chart.io, later chartio.com. The date of the move to chartio.com was not found. USPTO record shows CHARTIO filed in March 2016 and registered October 2016 to Chart.io, Inc.

brand_strength.rationale: Name clearly says what the product does and was easy to remember, but sources show no brand-driven growth, mascot or community beyond product coverage.

outcome_analysis: Chartio launched in mid 2010 as a cloud BI tool, raised small rounds with Avalon Ventures leading and had raised 6.64 million dollars in total by January 2014. It grew to about 40 people on the YC page and was acquired by Atlassian on 26 February 2021 for an undisclosed sum, with the product shut down on 1 March 2022 so the team could build analytics inside Atlassian products. The outcome was a modest strategic exit rather than a standalone breakout.
notes: SiliconANGLE states total raised 6.64 million dollars by January 2014. Aggregators list a seed of about 1 million dollars (May 2010) and a Series A of 3.15 to 4.4 million dollars led by Avalon with Bullpen Capital (2011 per one report); amounts conflict across aggregators, so those are unverified and not recorded as rounds. The 2014 round is described by sources as additional funding, so its stage is other. One aggregator wrongly names Salesforce as acquirer; Atlassian's own blog confirms Atlassian. Shutdown date conflicts between sources (1 January vs 1 March 2022); the homepage notice says 1 March 2022. Competitor list comes from search snippets of the August 2010 TechCrunch piece, which was not opened in full.
